prediction.raw: 0. I think it's wrong to pay someone to proofread your paper for college because it can be considered a form of academic dishonesty. In academic settings, it's essential to maintain the integrity of your work and ensure that the submissions are your own. While getting help with proofreading can be beneficial, paying someone to do it for you can be seen as outsourcing your responsibility and potentially misrepresenting your abilities. In college, the goal is not only to produce error-free work but also to learn and demonstrate your understanding of the subject matter. By paying someone to proofread your paper, you may be missing out on the opportunity to learn from your mistakes and develop your critical thinking and writing skills. Additionally, many colleges and universities have strict policies against academic dishonesty, and paying someone to proofread your work could be considered a violation of these policies. It's always best to seek help from your instructor, teaching assistant, or academic support services on campus, as they can provide guidance and support while maintaining the integrity of your work.
